content: The medication is indicated for the treatment of hospital-acquired bacterial pneumonia (HABP) and ventilator-associated bacterial pneumonia (VABP) caused by susceptible isolates of Acinetobacter baumannii-calcoaceticus complex (ABC). The recommended dosage is 2 grams (1 gram sulbactam and 1 gram durlobactam) administered intravenously every 6 hours, infused over a period of 3 hours. The duration of treatment is typically 7 to 14 days, but this should be adjusted based on the patient’s clinical status. This medication is not indicated for HABP/VABP caused by pathogens other than susceptible isolates of ABC. To minimize the development of drug-resistant bacteria and maintain the effectiveness of the treatment, it should only be used for infections that are proven or strongly suspected to be caused by bacteria. The safety and efficacy of this drug have not been fully established. Since the drug is substantially excreted by the kidneys, elderly patients, who are more likely to have reduced renal function, may require dosage adjustments based on their renal function. Coadministration of certain drugs can increase the plasma concentration of sulbactam/durlobactam due to interactions with transport proteins such as OATP1B1, OATP1B3, or OAT1. Examples of such drugs include: Ceftobiprole: Avoid or use an alternative drug, as it may increase sulbactam/durlobactam levels. Clarithromycin: Avoid or use an alternative drug, as it may increase sulbactam/durlobactam levels. Cyclosporine: Avoid or use an alternative drug, as it may increase sulbactam/durlobactam levels. Eluxadoline: Avoid or use an alternative drug, as it may increase sulbactam/durlobactam levels. Enasidenib: Avoid coadministration with sensitive substrates of OATP1B1, OATP1B3, or BCRP, as minimal concentration changes may lead to serious toxicities. If unavoidable, reduce the substrate dosage as per prescribing information. Erythromycin (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, stearate): Avoid or use an alternative drug, as it may increase sulbactam/durlobactam levels. Fostemsavir: Avoid or use an alternative drug, as it may increase sulbactam/durlobactam levels. Gemfibrozil: Avoid or use an alternative drug, as it may increase sulbactam/durlobactam levels. Glecaprevir/Pibrentasvir: Avoid or use an alternative drug, as it may increase sulbactam/durlobactam levels. Grapefruit: Avoid or use an alternative drug, as it may increase sulbactam/durlobactam levels. Lenolisib: Avoid or use an alternative drug, as it may increase sulbactam/durlobactam levels. Pazopanib: Avoid or use an alternative drug, as it may increase sulbactam/durlobactam levels. Pretomanid: Use caution and monitor closely for drug-related adverse effects if coadministered with sensitive OATP1B3 substrates. Rifampin and Rifamycin: Avoid or use an alternative drug, as they may increase sulbactam/durlobactam levels. Ritonavir: Avoid or use an alternative drug, as it may increase sulbactam/durlobactam levels. Sofosbuvir/Velpatasvir: Avoid or use an alternative drug, as it may increase sulbactam/durlobactam levels. Tacrolimus: Avoid or use an alternative drug, as it may increase sulbactam/durlobactam levels. Telmisartan: Avoid or use an alternative drug, as it may increase sulbactam/durlobactam levels. Trofinetide: Avoid or use an alternative drug, as it may increase sulbactam/durlobactam levels. Verapamil: Avoid or use an alternative drug, as it may increase sulbactam/durlobactam levels. Voxilaprevir: Avoid or use an alternative drug, as it may increase sulbactam/durlobactam levels. Sulbactam/durlobactam may also decrease the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors such as atezolizumab, avelumab, balstilimab, camrelizumab, cemiplimab, cosibelimab, dostarlimab, durvalumab, nivolumab, pembrolizumab, penpulimab, retifanlimab, sintilimab, tislelizumab, and toripalimab. Coadministration with these agents should be approached with caution, and close monitoring is recommended, as it may interfere with their therapeutic effects. Additionally, sulbactam/durlobactam may reduce the efficacy of oral microbiota products containing bacterial spores. It is recommended to complete antibiotic regimens 2 to 4 days before initiating oral microbiota therapy.
